verses.original: אֵ֭לֶּה גַּם־ מִשְׁלֵ֣י שְׁלֹמֹ֑ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר הֶ֝עְתִּ֗יקוּ אַנְשֵׁ֤י׀ חִזְקִיָּ֬ה מֶֽלֶךְ־ יְהוּדָֽה׃
verses.transliteration: ’êl·leh gam- miš·lê šə·lō·mōh ’ă·šer he‘·tî·qū ’an·šê ḥiz·qî·yāh me·leḵ- yə·hū·ḏāh
verses.literal: These [are] additional proverbs of Solomon which were copied by the men of Hezekiah king of Judah

verses.original: כְּבֹ֣ד אֱ֭לֹהִים הַסְתֵּ֣ר דָּבָ֑ר וּכְבֹ֥ד מְ֝לָכִ֗ים חֲקֹ֣ר דָּבָֽר׃
verses.transliteration: kə·ḇōḏ ’ĕ·lō·hîm has·têr dā·ḇār ū·ḵə·ḇōḏ mə·lā·ḵîm ḥă·qōr dā·ḇār
verses.literal: It is the glory of God to conceal a matter and the glory of kings to search it out . . .

verses.original: שָׁמַ֣יִם לָ֭רוּם וָאָ֣רֶץ לָעֹ֑מֶק וְלֵ֥ב מְ֝לָכִ֗ים אֵ֣ין חֵֽקֶר׃
verses.transliteration: šā·ma·yim lā·rūm wā·’ā·reṣ lā·‘ō·meq wə·lêḇ mə·lā·ḵîm ’ên ḥê·qer
verses.literal: As the heavens are high and the earth is deep so the hearts of kings cannot be searched

verses.original: הָג֣וֹ סִיגִ֣ים מִכָּ֑סֶף כֶּֽלִי׃ לַצֹּרֵ֣ף וַיֵּצֵ֖א
verses.transliteration: hā·ḡōw sî·ḡîm mik·kā·sep̄ ke·lî laṣ·ṣō·rêp̄ way·yê·ṣê
verses.literal: Remove the dross from the silver and a vessel for a silversmith will come forth

verses.original: הָג֣וֹ רָ֭שָׁע מֶ֑לֶךְ לִפְנֵי־ כִּסְאֽוֹ׃ וְיִכּ֖וֹן בַּצֶּ֣דֶק
verses.transliteration: hā·ḡōw rā·šā‘ me·leḵ lip̄·nê- kis·’ōw wə·yik·kō·wn baṣ·ṣe·ḏeq
verses.literal: Remove the wicked from the king’s presence and his throne will be established in righteousness

verses.original: אַל־ תִּתְהַדַּ֥ר לִפְנֵי־ מֶ֑לֶךְ אַֽל־ תַּעֲמֹֽד׃ וּבִמְק֥וֹם גְּ֝דֹלִ֗ים
verses.transliteration: ’al- tiṯ·had·dar lip̄·nê- me·leḵ ’al- ta·‘ă·mōḏ ū·ḇim·qō·wm gə·ḏō·lîm
verses.literal: Do not exalt yourself in the presence of the king and do not stand in the place of great [men]

verses.original: כִּ֤י ט֥וֹב אֲמָר־ לְךָ֗ עֲ‍ֽלֵ֫ה הֵ֥נָּה מֵֽ֭הַשְׁפִּ֣ילְךָ לִפְנֵ֣י נָדִ֑יב אֲשֶׁ֖ר רָא֣וּ עֵינֶֽיךָ׃
verses.transliteration: kî ṭō·wḇ ’ă·mār- lə·ḵā ‘ălêh hên·nāh mê·haš·pî·lə·ḵā lip̄·nê nā·ḏîḇ ’ă·šer rā·’ū ‘ê·ne·ḵā
verses.literal: for it is better to be told . . . Come up here than to be demoted in the presence of the prince Even what you have seen with your own eyes

verses.original: אַל־ תֵּצֵ֥א מַ֫הֵ֥ר לָרִ֗ב פֶּ֣ן מַה־ תַּ֭עֲשֶׂה בְּאַחֲרִיתָ֑הּ רֵעֶֽךָ׃ בְּהַכְלִ֖ים אֹתְךָ֣
verses.transliteration: ’al- tê·ṣê ma·hêr lā·riḇ pen mah- ta·‘ă·śeh bə·’a·ḥă·rî·ṯāh rê·‘e·ḵā bə·haḵ·lîm ’ō·ṯə·ḵā
verses.literal: do not bring hastily to court Otherwise what will you do in the end when your neighbor puts you to shame -

verses.original: רִֽ֭יבְךָ רִ֣יב אֶת־ רֵעֶ֑ךָ אַל־ תְּגָֽל׃ אַחֵ֣ר וְס֖וֹד
verses.transliteration: rî·ḇə·ḵā rîḇ ’eṯ- rê·‘e·ḵā ’al- tə·ḡāl ’a·ḥêr wə·sō·wḏ
verses.literal: Argue your case with your neighbor without betraying another’s confidence

verses.original: פֶּֽן־ שֹׁמֵ֑עַ יְחַסֶּדְךָ֥ וְ֝דִבָּתְךָ֗ לֹ֣א תָשֽׁוּב׃
verses.transliteration: pen- šō·mê·a‘ yə·ḥas·seḏ·ḵā wə·ḏib·bā·ṯə·ḵā lō ṯā·šūḇ
verses.literal: lest he who hears you bring shame upon you and your infamy never go away

verses.original: דָּ֝בָ֗ר עַל־ אָפְנָֽיו׃ דָּבֻ֥ר תַּפּוּחֵ֣י זָ֭הָב בְּמַשְׂכִּיּ֥וֹת כָּ֑סֶף
verses.transliteration: dā·ḇār ‘al- ’ā·p̄ə·nāw dā·ḇur tap·pū·ḥê zā·hāḇ bə·maś·kî·yō·wṯ kā·sep̄
verses.literal: A word vvv fitly spoken [is like] apples of gold in settings of silver

verses.original: נֶ֣זֶם זָ֭הָב וַחֲלִי־ כָ֑תֶם חָ֝כָ֗ם מוֹכִ֥יחַ עַל־ שֹׁמָֽעַת׃ אֹ֥זֶן
verses.transliteration: ne·zem zā·hāḇ wa·ḥă·lî- ḵā·ṯem ḥā·ḵām mō·w·ḵî·aḥ ‘al- šō·mā·‘aṯ ’ō·zen
verses.literal: [Like] an earring of gold or an ornament of fine gold is a wise man’s rebuke to a listening ear

verses.original: כְּצִנַּת־ שֶׁ֨לֶג׀ בְּי֬וֹם קָצִ֗יר נֶ֭אֱמָן צִ֣יר לְשֹׁלְחָ֑יו יָשִֽׁיב׃פ וְנֶ֖פֶשׁ אֲדֹנָ֣יו
verses.transliteration: kə·ṣin·naṯ- še·leḡ bə·yō·wm qā·ṣîr ne·’ĕ·mān ṣîr lə·šō·lə·ḥāw yā·šîḇ wə·ne·p̄eš ’ă·ḏō·nāw
verses.literal: Like the cold of snow in the time of harvest [is] a trustworthy messenger to those who send him he refreshes the soul of his masters

verses.original: נְשִׂיאִ֣ים וְ֭רוּחַ אָ֑יִן וְגֶ֣שֶׁם אִ֥ישׁ מִ֝תְהַלֵּ֗ל בְּמַתַּת־ שָֽׁקֶר׃
verses.transliteration: nə·śî·’îm wə·rū·aḥ ’ā·yin wə·ḡe·šem ’îš miṯ·hal·lêl bə·mat·taṯ- šā·qer
verses.literal: [Like] clouds and wind without rain [is] the man who boasts of gifts never given

verses.original: בְּאֹ֣רֶךְ אַ֭פַּיִם קָצִ֑ין יְפֻתֶּ֣ה רַ֝כָּ֗ה וְלָשׁ֥וֹן תִּשְׁבָּר־ גָּֽרֶם׃
verses.transliteration: bə·’ō·reḵ ’ap·pa·yim qā·ṣîn yə·p̄ut·teh rak·kāh wə·lā·šō·wn tiš·bār- gā·rem
verses.literal: Through patience . . . a ruler can be persuaded and a gentle tongue can break a bone

verses.original: מָ֭צָאתָ דְּבַ֣שׁ אֱכֹ֣ל דַּיֶּ֑ךָּ פֶּן־ תִּ֝שְׂבָּעֶ֗נּוּ וַהֲקֵֽאתֽוֹ׃
verses.transliteration: mā·ṣā·ṯā də·ḇaš ’ĕ·ḵōl day·ye·kā pen- tiś·bā·‘en·nū wa·hă·qê·ṯōw
verses.literal: If you find honey eat just what you need lest you have too much and vomit it up

verses.original: הֹקַ֣ר רַ֭גְלְךָ רֵעֶ֑ךָ מִבֵּ֣ית פֶּן־ יִ֝שְׂבָּעֲךָ֗ וּשְׂנֵאֶֽךָ׃
verses.transliteration: hō·qar raḡ·lə·ḵā rê·‘e·ḵā mib·bêṯ pen- yiś·bā·‘ă·ḵā ū·śə·nê·’e·ḵā
verses.literal: Seldom set foot in your neighbor’s house lest he grow weary and hate you

verses.original: מֵפִ֣יץ וְ֭חֶרֶב שָׁנ֑וּן וְחֵ֣ץ אִ֥ישׁ עֹנֶ֥ה שָֽׁקֶר׃ עֵ֣ד בְ֝רֵעֵ֗הוּ
verses.transliteration: mê·p̄îṣ wə·ḥe·reḇ šā·nūn wə·ḥêṣ ’îš ‘ō·neh šā·qer ‘êḏ ḇə·rê·‘ê·hū
verses.literal: [Like] a club or sword or sharp arrow [is] a man who bears false witness against his neighbor

verses.original: רֹ֭עָה שֵׁ֣ן וְרֶ֣גֶל מוּעָ֑דֶת מִבְטָ֥ח בּ֝וֹגֵ֗ד בְּי֣וֹם צָרָֽה׃
verses.transliteration: rō·‘āh šên wə·re·ḡel mū·‘ā·ḏeṯ miḇ·ṭāḥ bō·w·ḡêḏ bə·yō·wm ṣā·rāh
verses.literal: [Like] a broken tooth or a foot out of joint is confidence in a faithless man in time of trouble

verses.original: מַ֥עֲדֶה בֶּ֨גֶד׀ קָ֭רָה בְּי֣וֹם חֹ֣מֶץ עַל־ נָ֑תֶר וְשָׁ֥ר בַּ֝שִּׁרִ֗ים עַ֣ל רָֽע׃פ לֶב־
verses.transliteration: ma·‘ă·ḏeh be·ḡeḏ qā·rāh bə·yō·wm ḥō·meṣ ‘al- nā·ṯer wə·šār baš·ši·rîm ‘al rā‘ leḇ-
verses.literal: [Like] one who removes a garment on a cold day or vinegar poured on a wound [is] one who sings songs to a heavy heart

verses.original: אִם־ שֹׂ֭נַאֲךָ רָעֵ֣ב לָ֑חֶם הַאֲכִלֵ֣הוּ וְאִם־ צָ֝מֵ֗א מָֽיִם׃ הַשְׁקֵ֥הוּ
verses.transliteration: ’im- śō·na·ʾă·k̲ā rā·‘êḇ lā·ḥem ha·’ă·ḵi·lê·hū wə·’im- ṣā·mê mā·yim haš·qê·hū
verses.literal: If your enemy is hungry give him food to eat and if he is thirsty give him water to drink

verses.original: כִּ֤י אַ֭תָּה חֹתֶ֣ה גֶֽחָלִ֗ים עַל־ רֹאשׁ֑וֹ וַֽ֝יהוָ֗ה יְשַׁלֶּם־ לָֽךְ׃
verses.transliteration: kî ’at·tāh ḥō·ṯeh ḡe·ḥā·lîm ‘al- rō·šōw Yah·weh yə·šal·lem- lāḵ
verses.literal: For [in so doing] you will heap burning coals on his head and the LORD will reward you

verses.original: צָ֭פוֹן ר֣וּחַ תְּח֣וֹלֵֽל גָּ֑שֶׁם סָֽתֶר׃ לְשׁ֣וֹן נִ֝זְעָמִ֗ים וּפָנִ֥ים
verses.transliteration: ṣā·p̄ō·wn rū·aḥ tə·ḥō·w·lêl gā·šem sā·ṯer lə·šō·wn niz·‘ā·mîm ū·p̄ā·nîm
verses.literal: As the north wind brings forth rain so a backbiting tongue [brings] angry looks

verses.original: ט֗וֹב שֶׁ֥בֶת עַל־ פִּנַּת־ גָּ֑ג חָֽבֶר׃ וּבֵ֥ית מְדוֹנִים מֵאֵ֥שֶׁת
verses.transliteration: ṭō·wḇ še·ḇeṯ ‘al- pin·naṯ- gāḡ ḥā·ḇer ū·ḇêṯ mə·ḏō·nīm mê·’ê·šeṯ
verses.literal: Better to live on a corner of the roof than to share a house with a quarrelsome wife

verses.original: קָ֭רִים מַ֣יִם עַל־ עֲיֵפָ֑ה נֶ֣פֶשׁ ט֝וֹבָ֗ה וּשְׁמוּעָ֥ה מֶרְחָֽק׃ מֵאֶ֥רֶץ
verses.transliteration: qā·rîm ma·yim ‘al- ‘ă·yê·p̄āh ne·p̄eš ṭō·w·ḇāh ū·šə·mū·‘āh mer·ḥāq mê·’e·reṣ
verses.literal: [Like] cold water to a weary soul [is] good news from a distant land

verses.original: נִ֭רְפָּשׂ מַעְיָ֣ן מָשְׁחָ֑ת וּמָק֣וֹר צַ֝דִּ֗יק מָ֣ט לִפְנֵֽי־ רָשָֽׁע׃
verses.transliteration: nir·pāś ma‘·yān mā·šə·ḥāṯ ū·mā·qō·wr ṣad·dîq māṭ lip̄·nê- rā·šā‘
verses.literal: Like a muddied spring or a polluted well is a righteous man who gives way to the wicked

verses.original: לֹא־ ט֑וֹב אָ֘כֹ֤ל הַרְבּ֣וֹת דְּבַ֣שׁ וְחֵ֖קֶר כְּבֹדָ֣ם כָּבֽוֹד׃
verses.transliteration: lō- ṭō·wḇ ’ā·ḵōl har·bō·wṯ də·ḇaš wə·ḥê·qer kə·ḇō·ḏām kā·ḇō·wḏ
verses.literal: It is not good to eat too much honey or to search out one’s own glory . . .

verses.original: עִ֣יר חוֹמָ֑ה פְּ֭רוּצָה אִ֝֗ישׁ אֲשֶׁ֤ר אֵ֖ין אֵ֣ין מַעְצָ֣ר לְרוּחֽוֹ׃
verses.transliteration: ‘îr ḥō·w·māh pə·rū·ṣāh ’îš ’ă·šer ’ên ’ên ma‘·ṣār lə·rū·ḥōw
verses.literal: Like a city whose walls are broken down is a man who . . . does not control his temper
